cluster_name: Salmonella jalapeño outbreak and US avocado inspection halt in Michoacán
tldr: The headline layer of this cluster splits across two US-Mexico food-safety stories: eight of eleven titles frame a salmonella outbreak traced to Mexican jalapeños in a uniform HEALTH_SAFETY register, while three advertise the US suspension of avocado inspections in Michoacán through a SECURITY_DEFENSE frame tied to cartel violence. The most striking divergence is RT's pivot away from both dominant stories to lead with 'diarrhea-inducing parasite' deaths — sensationalized framing of an unrelated Cyclospora outbreak that appears nowhere else in the corpus. The Independent advertises the avocado suspension as a 'cartel stronghold' threat to US food security, the most alarmist phrasing in the corpus; Reuters covers the identical event with neutral 'security alert' language. Several outlets — Hindustan Times, Straits Times, one Reuters article — converge on near-identical phrasing ('Mexican jalapenos tied to Salmonella outbreak'), producing a bloc of minimal frame differentiation that makes this cluster's international jalapeño coverage unusually homogeneous at the headline layer.
event_summary: US authorities linked a salmonella outbreak sickening 345 people across 27 states to Mexican jalapeños, with Chipotle and Qdoba removing them from menus; the US also suspended avocado export inspections in Michoacán following a security threat against US personnel.

silences.what_they_covered_instead: RT's headline leads with confirmed US deaths from a 'diarrhea-inducing parasite' (Cyclospora), a story entirely absent from every other title in the corpus; the cluster-dominant jalapeño salmonella story does not appear in RT's headline at all.

single_outlet_findings.finding: Only headline to pivot entirely to a different outbreak — Cyclospora parasite deaths framed as 'diarrhea-inducing' — rather than the cluster-dominant jalapeño salmonella story, advertising maximum alarm with a story invisible in all other titles.

Only headline to frame the Michoacán avocado suspension as a cartel threat to US food security ('A cartel stronghold just put America's avocado supply at risk'), the most alarmist language in the corpus for an event Reuters covers as a neutral 'security alert.'

bottom_line: At the headline layer, the jalapeño salmonella story dominates in a uniform HEALTH_SAFETY frame across seven outlets from six countries, producing unusually homogeneous international coverage with several outlets using near-identical phrasing. The avocado sub-story generates the sharpest headline divergence: The Independent frames it as a cartel threat to US food security while Reuters uses neutral regulatory language for the same event. RT stands entirely apart from the cluster by advertising a Cyclospora parasite death toll instead of either dominant story, a headline that would mislead a reader about what this cluster actually covers.
